reads.about:
# Android Computer Use MCP

Purpose:
- Provide a structured Android execution substrate for emulator lifecycle, app control, observation, semantic UI interaction, raw input fallback, and Solar Lab scenarios.

Current posture:
- Hosted interactive-session tools can reuse a live runner-backed emulator without rebuilding or rebooting it for each new APK.
- Semantic Android tools are the preferred interaction lane.
- Raw input tools remain available as fallback when semantic selection is insufficient.
- Optional scenario tools provide durable examples above the generic Android surface.

Contract:
- Public tool exposure is governed by explicit tool inventory registration.
- Discovery resources are read-only and intended for cold-start orientation.
- Tool schema and resource catalog snapshots guard the public contract.
reads.help:
# Android Computer Use MCP help

Recommended interaction order:
1. interactive_session.get_status when working against a hosted runner-backed session.
2. android.health or android.list_devices to understand the current harness state.
3. android.wait_for_boot if a device may still be starting.
4. interactive_session.install_build_from_run to swap a fresh remote-built APK into a live hosted session.
5. android.launch_app or a Solar Lab scenario to reach the target surface.
6. android.wait_for_stable_ui before acting through semantic UI tools.
7. android.tap_element or android.type_into_element for semantic interaction.
8. android.input.* only when semantic tools are insufficient.

Guidance:
- Prefer semantic UI tools over raw input whenever a selector can describe the target.
- Prefer scenario tools for durable Solar Lab flows instead of rebuilding them ad hoc.
- Use observation tools when you need artifacts or structured state, not just one action.

Hosted usage notes:
- This server works well as a runner-backed Android substrate over Streamable HTTP.
- interactive_session.* tools exist to avoid restarting the hosted runner for each new build.
- Discovery resources exist so a fresh agent can orient without local repo context.

notes: Scenario tools are the preferred entry points for durable Solar Lab validation flows.
Use solarlab.semantic_action for bounded domain actions when a full scenario is too broad.

scenarios.description: Launch Solar Lab, open search, focus Earth, and capture step-by-step artifacts.
scenarios.name: solarlab.scenario.stage_first_focus_earth
scenarios.use_when: Use this to run a durable Stage First Solar Lab scenario rather than reassembling the flow by hand.

scenarios.description: Launch Solar Lab, open immersive view, return to sandbox, and capture artifacts.
scenarios.name: solarlab.scenario.stage_first_immersive_roundtrip
scenarios.use_when: Use this to validate the immersive roundtrip flow with consistent artifact capture.

scenarios.description: Send a narrow semantic action into the Solar Lab app and optionally capture post-action screenshot and UI artifacts.
scenarios.name: solarlab.semantic_action
scenarios.use_when: Use this for narrow Solar Lab domain actions when a full scenario would be too broad.

tools.description: Report hosted interactive-session configuration, live session root, and active build metadata.
tools.name: interactive_session.get_status
tools.use_when: Use this first when you need to understand the current hosted runner-backed session before switching builds.

tools.description: Read the current active-build metadata for the hosted interactive session.
tools.name: interactive_session.get_current_build
tools.use_when: Use this when you want the exact build currently installed without changing live session state.

tools.description: Download a reusable interactive build artifact from a GitHub Actions run, install it into the live session, and optionally relaunch the app.
tools.name: interactive_session.install_build_from_run
tools.use_when: Use this to swap a newly built APK into an already-live hosted session instead of restarting the runner.

tools.description: Relaunch the current active build inside the live hosted interactive session.
tools.name: interactive_session.relaunch_current_build
tools.use_when: Use this for a cheap retry loop when the active build is already installed and only needs relaunch.

tools.description: Report SDK paths, known AVDs, and attached Android devices.
tools.name: android.health
tools.use_when: Use this first to understand the local Android harness posture before taking action.

tools.description: List known local Android virtual devices.
tools.name: android.list_avds
tools.use_when: Use this when you need to choose or verify an AVD name before launch.

tools.description: List adb-visible Android devices.
tools.name: android.list_devices
tools.use_when: Use this when you need the current device serials or want to confirm device visibility.

tools.description: Resolve one exact Android provider, session, and device target.
tools.name: android.resolve_target
tools.use_when: Use this before a target-bound Android operation to reject a stale or mismatched provider session.

tools.description: Launch a named AVD in the background.
tools.name: android.launch_avd
tools.use_when: Use this to start an emulator when no suitable device is already running.

tools.description: Launch a named AVD, wait for its emulator serial to appear, and verify boot readiness.
tools.name: android.launch_avd_and_wait
tools.use_when: Use this when you want one bounded boot flow instead of separate launch and boot checks.

tools.description: Wait until sys.boot_completed=1 and package manager is responsive.
tools.name: android.wait_for_boot
tools.use_when: Use this after launch when the device exists but may not be ready for app work yet.

tools.description: Install an APK onto the target device.
tools.name: android.install_apk
tools.use_when: Use this when the app under test is not already installed or needs updating.

tools.description: Launch an installed Android app by package name and optional activity.
tools.name: android.launch_app
tools.use_when: Use this to bring an app to the foreground before semantic UI interaction.

tools.description: List installed Android apps, optionally limited to launcher-visible apps.
tools.name: android.list_apps
tools.use_when: Use this when you need package names before launching, terminating, or uninstalling apps.

tools.description: Force-stop an installed Android app by package name.
tools.name: android.terminate_app
tools.use_when: Use this to reset app state without uninstalling it.

tools.description: Uninstall an Android app by package name.
tools.name: android.uninstall_app
tools.use_when: Use this only when the app should be removed from the device.

tools.description: Open an http:// or https:// URL on the Android device.
tools.name: android.open_url
tools.use_when: Use this when the browser or URL intent path is the task under test.

tools.description: Read the device user_rotation setting and normalized orientation class.
tools.name: android.get_orientation
tools.use_when: Use this to record orientation before choosing gestures or validation expectations.

tools.description: Set the device user_rotation after disabling accelerometer rotation.
tools.name: android.set_orientation
tools.use_when: Use this when validation needs a known portrait or landscape posture.

tools.description: Capture a PNG screenshot from the device and save it locally.
tools.name: android.capture_screenshot
tools.use_when: Use this when a visual artifact is more important than the normalized UI tree.

tools.description: Dump the current UI hierarchy XML and save it locally.
tools.name: android.dump_ui_hierarchy
tools.use_when: Use this when you need raw hierarchy XML for debugging or later parsing.

tools.description: Read a previously generated artifact file from the configured artifact directory and return its contents for remote consumers.
tools.name: android.read_artifact
tools.use_when: Use this when a remote consumer needs the bytes or text for a screenshot, UI dump, or other artifact path that was returned earlier.

tools.description: Capture the current UI hierarchy, optionally pair it with a screenshot, and return a normalized UI tree.
tools.name: android.inspect_ui
tools.use_when: Use this for a rich one-shot observation of the current Android state.

tools.description: Wait until the UI hierarchy and top window state stop changing, then return a paired observation bundle.
tools.name: android.wait_for_stable_ui
tools.use_when: Use this before acting when the UI may still be animating or transitioning.

tools.description: Find the first normalized UI element matching a semantic selector in the current hierarchy.
tools.name: android.find_ui_element
tools.use_when: Use this to inspect whether a target control is present and how it resolved before acting.

tools.description: Wait until a semantic UI selector is present or absent in the current hierarchy.
tools.name: android.wait_for_ui_element
tools.use_when: Use this when a UI transition is expected and success depends on a selector appearing or disappearing.

tools.description: Find a semantic UI element and tap its center point.
tools.name: android.tap_element
tools.use_when: Use this as the default interaction path when you can describe the target semantically.

tools.description: Find a semantic UI element, tap it, and send text input.
tools.name: android.type_into_element
tools.use_when: Use this for text entry into a known field when semantic targeting is available.

tools.description: Swipe the viewport until a semantic UI selector becomes visible or the swipe budget is exhausted.
tools.name: android.scroll_until_visible
tools.use_when: Use this when the target probably exists off-screen and semantic scrolling is preferable to raw swipes.

tools.description: Capture recent logcat output and save it locally.
tools.name: android.collect_logcat
tools.use_when: Use this after a failure or suspicious behavior when app/runtime logs matter.

tools.description: Send a tap input event to the device.
tools.name: android.input.tap
tools.use_when: Use this only when semantic selection is insufficient and you already know the screen coordinates.

tools.description: Send a double-tap input event to the device as one bounded gesture.
tools.name: android.input.double_tap
tools.use_when: Use this only when a genuine Android double-tap gesture is needed and semantic interaction is insufficient.

tools.description: Send a long-press input event to the device as one bounded gesture.
tools.name: android.input.long_press
tools.use_when: Use this only when a genuine Android long-press gesture is needed and semantic interaction is insufficient.

tools.description: Send text input to the device.
tools.name: android.input.text
tools.use_when: Use this when raw keyboard-style entry is required after focus is already established.

tools.description: Send a swipe gesture to the device.
tools.name: android.input.swipe
tools.use_when: Use this only when semantic scrolling is insufficient or you need an exact gesture path.

tools.description: Send two to five pointer paths as one atomic emulator gRPC gesture.
tools.name: android.input.multi_touch
tools.use_when: Use this for pinch, two-finger pan, or another gesture that must keep every pointer in the same device frame.

tools.description: Send a keyevent to the device.
tools.name: android.input.keyevent
tools.use_when: Use this for bounded low-level actions like Back or Enter when semantic tools are not the right fit.

tools.description: Send a chorded key combination to the device.
tools.name: android.input.keycombination
tools.use_when: Use this for computer-use key chords such as Ctrl+C that must be dispatched atomically.

tools.description: Launch Solar Lab, open search, focus Earth, and capture step-by-step artifacts.
tools.name: solarlab.scenario.stage_first_focus_earth
tools.use_when: Use this to run a durable Stage First Solar Lab scenario rather than reassembling the flow by hand.

tools.description: Launch Solar Lab, open immersive view, return to sandbox, and capture artifacts.
tools.name: solarlab.scenario.stage_first_immersive_roundtrip
tools.use_when: Use this to validate the immersive roundtrip flow with consistent artifact capture.

tools.description: Send a narrow semantic action into the Solar Lab app and optionally capture post-action screenshot and UI artifacts.
tools.name: solarlab.semantic_action
tools.use_when: Use this for narrow Solar Lab domain actions when a full scenario would be too broad.
